correctness.rationale: Adding the two ordered sampling probabilities gives the stated positive q_ij. Edge 13 is initially inactive. Ignoring null draws, the first receptive edge has the stated conditional law, and either produces a coincident pair separated by a gap at least c from the remaining agent (an absorbing state), or leaves diameter <c. Without a strict initial bridge an averaging of the only receptive edge increases the former isolated gap, so consensus is impossible. On the all-receptive branch, the mean is conserved; also, independently of the variance proof, each disjoint block of draws (12,23) contracts the diameter by at least one half, and such blocks occur infinitely often almost surely. The first-left and first-right consensus windows reduce to (2(1−c),c) and (1−c,2c−1), respectively. They are nonempty precisely for c>2/3 and intersect precisely for c>3/4, giving the exact maxima and strict boundary values. At c=4/5 the two stated mirror profiles select opposite branches, and the ratio of q12 to q23 is a(a+3)/4. The resulting numerators and strict opposite activity monotonicity follow.
residual_risks: The checker covers 23670 rational comparisons and threshold identities, not the infinite-time convergence. The review verifies convergence analytically and does not assert finite-time exact consensus.

originality.rationale: The contribution retained is the complete, fixed-profile terminal law with sharp confidence windows and the exact activity-placement reversal in the node-first complete-triad model. Li–Porter already give the sampling and update dynamics, and the later-labeled indexed path theorem duplicates the mechanism and conditional consensus probability in the both-receptive branch after effective-event conditioning. It does not give the whole complete-triad law or the explicit dependence on node activity and mirrored initial opinions. This is not credit for a novel sampling rule, first-event decomposition or general consensus convergence. No inspected pre-existing or broader result gives the full contribution; publication priority is not certified.
residual_risks: The 2D repulsion/Poisson precedent described by Li–Porter was not read at its original source; it is only a reported qualitative antecedent here.

An older exact small-confidence-network analysis or equivalent account conditioned on three deterministic initial opinions is not excluded. The catalogue date of the path record does not establish priority.

value.rationale: An exact terminal distribution in the smallest complete graph with two competing effective edges distinguishes when the dynamics cannot reach consensus, can reach it with an activity-dependent probability, or can be made certain by choosing the middle opinion. The opposing activity effect is a useful exact witness that an aggregate fragmentation trend need not hold under conditioning on opinion placement. The value is this quantified boundary and counterexample, not just checking a three-agent simulation.
residual_risks: This does not prescribe activity effects on random populations, larger graphs or compromise fractions below one half. Confidence equalities depend on the strict test.
